title: U.S. House · Arkansas's 4th District
area: South Arkansas, including Pine Bluff, El Dorado, Hot Springs, and Texarkana.

context.text: Incumbent Bruce Westerman's Republican primary was canceled after only he qualified. James Russell defeated Steven O'Donnell in the Democratic primary.

summary.text: Bruce Westerman is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 4th District, seeking re-election. An engineer and forester from Hot Springs, he served on a school board and in the Arkansas House of Representatives, including as House Majority Leader, before being elected to Congress in 2014. He chairs the House Natural Resources Committee and also serves on Transportation and Infrastructure.

background.text: According to his official House biography, he is a Hot Springs native who graduated from Fountain Lake High School in Garland County and is a husband and father of four.

Attended the University of Arkansas, where he played on the Razorback football team, and earned a bachelor's degree in biological and agricultural engineering in 1990; he earned a Master of Forestry from Yale University in 2001.
Worked as a plant engineer for Riceland Foods and as an engineer and forester for Mid-South Engineering Company; his House biography says he spent 22 years at Mid-South Engineering in Hot Springs.
Served on the Fountain Lake School Board from 2006 to 2010, including as president in 2009-2010.

Served in the Arkansas House of Representatives from 2011 to 2014, as House Minority Leader (2012-2013) and then House Majority Leader (2013-2014); his House biography says he was the state's first Republican House Majority Leader since Reconstruction.
Won election to the U.S. House in 2014, succeeding Tom Cotton, and has served since January 2015.
Serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and is Chairman of the Committee on Natural Resources.

priorities.text: It is a great privilege to serve as the Chairman of the House Committee on Natural Resources. In this committee, the stewardship of our public lands remains a top priority for all its members.

In November, the American people voted to put America first. Today, Congress delivered on that promise... House and Senate Republicans have passed a reconciliation package that unleashes American energy, provides lower tax rates for all Americans, secures our borders, strengthens our nation's military capabilities, and roots out government waste, fraud, and abuse.

positions.summary: Cosponsored legislation to permanently repeal the federal estate tax on inherited farms and businesses, and backed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act making the 2017 tax cuts permanent.
positions.quote: I'm proud to cosponsor the Death Tax Repeal Act, with overwhelming support from my colleagues on both sides of the aisle, to fully repeal the death tax.

positions.summary: Backed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's border security funding, including wall completion and additional Border Patrol agents.
positions.quote: Secures the border: Expands border security through completion of the primary wall across the southern border and river barriers.

record.text: Currently chairs the House Committee on Natural Resources and serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
Cosponsored the Death Tax Repeal Act, which would permanently repeal the federal estate tax on transfers of family farms and small businesses.

summary.text: James Russell is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 4th Congressional District. He is a business owner who has worked in statewide mental healthcare since 2014, ran unsuccessfully for the Democratic nomination for governor in 2022, and describes deep family ties to Arkansas farming going back to the 1860s.

background.text: Ballotpedia says he has lived in Little Rock; he graduated from Captain Shreve High School and earned bachelor's degrees from the University of Central Arkansas in 2012 (a B.S. in philosophy) and 2021.
Served in the U.S. Army National Guard in 1996.
Career experience includes owning CYA Music, LLC, co-owning New Dawn Counseling, and working as a musician; says he has provided statewide mental healthcare services since 2014.
In his Ballotpedia survey, describes his family as having farmed in Lafayette County, Arkansas since the 1860s and says he worked with youth groups in Columbia County in the 1990s.
Ran in the May 24, 2022 Democratic primary for Arkansas governor, which Chris Jones won.
Describes himself as a husband, father, uncle and great-uncle who studied a joint pre-med/pre-law curriculum at the University of Central Arkansas.

priorities.text: Says leaders should listen to and be accountable to the people rather than to money and power, and calls for following the Constitution.
priorities.quote: Leaders should listen to the people, not hide from them. They should go to town halls, not just big money events.

priorities.text: Supports equal rights and opportunities regardless of gender, income, or background, including fair pay and bodily autonomy.
Wants to address the housing crisis by curbing large investors' home purchases and letting renters' payment history count toward mortgage qualification.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for restricting large corporate purchases of homes and helping renters qualify for mortgages, rather than broad deregulation of zoning.
positions.quote: We need to stop big companies from buying up homes and raising rent too high. We should also count rent payments when people apply for a mortgage, so more folks can buy a home.

positions.summary: Campaign platform proposes a small tax on the wealthiest 0.1% to help fund efforts to end homelessness.
positions.quote: By adding a small tax on the super-rich—the top 0.1%—we can help end homelessness for good.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for investing in a clean-energy future using multiple sources and protecting natural resources from industrial pollution.
positions.quote: We need to invest in a clean energy future that uses multiple sources to stay safe and strong.
